methods.name: Remove the seasons (monthly anomalies)
methods.description: Subtract the average of each calendar month so summer/winter is not mistaken for a trend.

methods.name: Theil-Sen slope with 95% confidence interval
methods.description: A robust slope - the median of the slopes between all pairs of months.

methods.name: Mann-Kendall test with Hamed-Rao correction
methods.description: Is the trend real or luck? Corrected because each month resembles the previous one.

methods.name: Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate
methods.description: Testing hundreds of cells makes some look significant by chance; FDR corrects for it.

methods.name: Regional average weighted by cos(latitude)
methods.description: One series for the whole area, then the same slope and test.

methods.name: Years needed to detect the trend (Weatherhead 1998)
methods.description: For non-significant trends, how many years of data would be needed to be sure.

methods.name: Rank variables by significant area
methods.description: Which variable changes over the largest share of the area.

methods.name: Opposite-trend map and sub-region contrasts
methods.description: Find places moving in opposite directions that a regional average would hide.

methods.name: Trend-signature clusters (k-means, silhouette)
methods.description: Group cells that changed in a similar way. Clusters suggest, statistics decide.

answer:
## Short answer

Yes, the Levant is getting hotter, and its soil is drying out. Air temperature increased significantly across the entire region from 2001-01 to 2024-12. Over the same period, topsoil moisture showed a significant decrease, while rainfall showed a slight decrease that is not statistically significant. At the same time, plant greenness showed a significant increase.

## What the data shows

A trend is a direction of change over time. An anomaly is the difference between an observed monthly value and its long-term average for that month. When scientists say a result is significant, they mean the pattern is unlikely to occur by random chance alone, defined here by a p-value of 0.05 or less. The slope measures the speed and direction of the change per decade.

- Air temperature at 2 m has a regional slope of 0.453 degC per decade over the period 2001-01 to 2024-12 [observed]. This upward trend has a p-value of < 0.001 and is significant [observed]. A significant increase was found across 100 percent of the area, while 0 percent showed a decrease, across 40 cells tested [observed].
- Soil moisture (0-10 cm) has a regional slope of -0.174 kg m-2 per decade over the period 2001-01 to 2024-12 [observed]. This downward trend has a p-value of 0.045 and is significant [observed]. A significant decrease occurred across 39.1 percent of the area, while 7.7 percent showed a significant increase, across 40 cells tested [observed].
- Precipitation has a regional slope of -0.454 mm/month per decade over the period 2001-01 to 2024-12 [observed]. This trend has a p-value of 0.29 and is not significant [observed]. Across 40 cells tested, 0 percent of the area showed a significant increase and 4.9 percent showed a significant decrease [observed].
- Vegetation greenness (NDVI) has a regional slope of 0.00456 NDVI units per decade over the period 2001-01 to 2024-12 [observed]. This upward trend has a p-value of 0.024 and is significant [observed]. A significant increase occurred across 65.3 percent of the area, and 0 percent showed a significant decrease, across 40 cells tested [observed].

## What scientists have written

- Warmer air temperatures can lead to higher evaporation rates [literature]. In the study "Evidence of increasing drought severity caused by temperature rise in southern Europe" (2014), researchers noted "greater atmospheric evaporative demand resulting from temperature rise" [literature].

## Possible explanations

No specific hypotheses were provided in the evidence pack. Observed connections between temperature and drying are correlations and do not prove causation.

## Limits of this investigation

- The data covers the period from 2001-01 to 2024-12. This time span may not capture longer climate cycles.
- The rainfall decrease is not statistically significant. Detecting a significant trend at this rate would require 87.8 years of data.
- Soil moisture measurements only represent the top layer of ground from 0-10 cm. They do not show deeper water storage.
- Correlation is not causation. A warming trend occurring at the same time as drying soil does not by itself prove one caused the other.
